Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the rapid response from Redwood during the disruption on Oct 18. We had several downstream async jobs and a handful of production endpoints that experienced elevated error rates; our SREs mitigated the immediate customer impact, but our leadership is asking for a clear, concise summary we can share internally.

Could you please send: 1) a short timeline of what happened and when, 2) the engineering root cause and contributing factors, and 3) the practical, customer-facing actions and owners for any follow-up items (including compensatory timelines if required). A PDF or spreadsheet would be great.

We appreciate the partnership — we want to close this loop with auditors and our compliance team by next Friday.

Thanks,
Jordan

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear ask and for the signal from your SREs. We pulled together an initial readout below and are preparing a formal package (PDF + timeline CSV + action checklist) that I will deliver by Friday 10/22. High-level summary first, then next steps and owners.

Short summary (executive):
- Impact: elevated 5xx rates across inference endpoints for ~28 minutes beginning at 03:18 UTC on 10/18; automatic fallbacks prevented broader consumer impact but several merchant async jobs saw retries.
- Root cause (short): an automated kernel-selection job incorrectly selected a non-quantized kernel variant for a small slice of models during a rolling config rollout, causing increased memory pressure and KV-cache evictions on a subset of serving hosts.
- Customer action: none required to restore service; proposed follow-ups include verification steps on your side and a review of any failed job retries.

Planned deliverables (arriving by 10/22):
1) Full narrative PDF: sequence of events and remediation narrative.
2) Incident timeline CSV: event timestamps, impacted hosts, request samples (anonymized).
3) Action checklist XLSX: owners, ETA, verification steps, and confirmation criteria.

Immediate internal actions we are taking now:
- Reverted the kernel-selection rollout and applied a safeguard to the rollout orchestration (owner: david_kim — ETA: 10/20 EOD).
- Added additional telemetry filters to detect kernel-selection anomalies earlier (owner: karthik_iyer — ETA: 10/21).

I will send the full packet once the technical appendices are finalized. If you need anything sooner (e.g., direct access to filtered logs), tell me and we can set up a secure share.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

Subject: Final delivery: Oct 18 disruption — incident readout, timeline, and action checklist

Jordan / Samantha —

Attached is the formal incident packet we promised: a concise narrative (PDF), a machine-readable timeline (CSV), and an action checklist (XLSX). Key points up front for your execs and auditors, followed by concrete next steps.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
On 2026-10-18 at 03:18 UTC Redwood experienced a 28-minute degradation in inference availability for a small fraction of model-serving hosts. The immediate cause was an automated kernel-selection rollout that, under specific model-version and batch-size combinations, selected a memory-inefficient kernel variant. This increased memory pressure on affected GPUs, triggered KV-cache evictions, and led to elevated 5xx responses from the serving layer. We reverted the rollout, applied rollout-guard checks, and validated recovery across affected customers within 36 minutes; no customer data was exposed.

Timeline highlights (see attached CSV for full detail):
- 03:18 UTC: first spike in 5xx observed; automated alert fired.
- 03:21 UTC: initial mitigation — traffic routed to fallback model variant; error rate partially reduced.
- 03:34 UTC: rollback of kernel-selection rollout initiated.
- 03:46 UTC: KV-cache sizes normalized; metrics returned to baseline by 03:46 UTC.

Root cause and contributing factors:
- Root cause: rollout automation selected a kernel variant incompatible with a small class of quantized checkpoints; the compatibility matrix did not include this path.
- Contributing factors: incomplete orchestration guards for kernel-variant selection; insufficient telemetry on memory fragmentation patterns; canary batch sizes were larger than ideal for this model family.

Customer-facing action items and owners (attached XLSX):
- Action 1: Provide Acme with impacted host list and anonymized request samples for internal verification — owner: david_kim — ETA: 10/23 (complete).
- Action 2: Joint verification window (staging traffic replay) — owner: karthik_iyer / Acme SREs — proposed dates: 10/26-10/27.
- Action 3: Deploy rollout-guard checks (compatibility matrix enforcement) and reduce canary batch size — owner: infra-release — ETA: 10/29.
- Action 4: Add telemetry for memory fragmentation and pre-eviction alerts — owner: karthik_iyer — ETA: 10/21 (deployed).

Compensation and SLAs:
We recognize the operational impact to Acme. We're open to discussing a small credit for the impacted window; I've cc'd our account team to start that conversation if you prefer.

Next steps:
- Please confirm a joint verification window that works for your SREs.
- Let us know if the delivered artifacts satisfy your audit needs or if you require additional redaction/formatting.

Files attached: 20261022-acme-rca-summary.pdf, 20261022-incident-timeline.csv, 20261022-action-checklist.xlsx

If you want a short walkthrough, I'm happy to schedule a 30-minute readout next week and include David and Karthik for technical Q&A.

Appreciate the partnership — we'll follow through until you're comfortable closing the ticket.

Best regards,
Evelyn Hart
